title: Refined lower logarithmic ratio
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, and let $r,p\in\mathbb R$. Define the refined lower logarithmic ratio by $\log q_f(p)-(1-r)\log p$, where $q_f(p)$ is the polynomial biased probability that $f$ outputs $-1$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps sign vectors of length $n$ to signs
caveat: This definition uses the polynomial biased minus probability, whose upstream definitions and bias convention are not supplied.
